ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic word أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا (ahlan wa sahlan) mean? (1 mark)
   A. welcome
   B. I
   C. I am well
   D. good morning (the reply)

2. What does the mark shadda tell you in the word umm? (1 mark)
   A. The vowel is long
   B. The letter is silent
   C. The letter mim is said twice
   D. The word is a question

3. Which word means 'above'? (1 mark)
   A. taHta
   B. fii
   C. fawqa
   D. ʿalaa

4. What does the Arabic word بَيْتٌ (bayt) mean? (1 mark)
   A. house
   B. book
   C. pen
   D. kitchen

5. How is the Arabic word اِسْمَعْ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ismaʿ
   B. ijlis
   C. aghmiD ʿaynayka
   D. ukhruj

6. What does the Arabic sentence فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I play on Saturday.
   B. There are seven days in a week.
   C. Today is Thursday.
   D. I go to school on Monday.

7. What does the Arabic word بَالُونٌ (baaluun) mean? (1 mark)
   A. juice
   B. candle
   C. song
   D. balloon

8. What does the Arabic sentence هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like bananas.
   B. I drink water.
   C. Do you like bananas?
   D. I eat bread.

9. How is the Arabic word أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. uktub
   B. ismaʿ
   C. aghmiD ʿaynayka
   D. ilmis anfaka

10. What does the Arabic word ادْخُلْ (udkhul) mean? (1 mark)
   A. listen
   B. come in
   C. close your eyes
   D. open the door

11. What does the Arabic sentence كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is hot.
   B. The weather is cold.
   C. The weather is rainy.
   D. How is the weather today?

12. What does the Arabic sentence الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is hot.
   B. The weather is cold.
   C. The water is clean.
   D. The weather is rainy.

13. What is the name of the Arabic letter ن? (1 mark)
   A. nuun
   B. waaw
   C. shiin
   D. taa

14. How do you read the syllable نِ? (1 mark)
   A. buu
   B. muu
   C. la
   D. ni

15. Which letter has three dots above it? (1 mark)
   A. ت (taa)
   B. ب (baa)
   C. ج (jiim)
   D. ث (thaa)

16. Which Arabic sentence means "I visit my grandmother on Friday." (1 mark)
   A. أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ
   B. أَنَا مِنْ كينيا
   C. أَقْرَأُ كِتَابًا يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ
   D. أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ

17. How is the Arabic word دَوْرُكَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. dawruka
   B. mabruuk
   C. ʿasiir
   D. kaʿka

18. Which Arabic sentence means "Above the table there is a balloon." (1 mark)
   A. هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ
   B. الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ
   C. فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ بَالُونٌ
   D. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كَعْكَةٌ

19. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. On the table there is a cake.
   B. The friends are at the party.
   C. This is a party.
   D. Above the table there is a balloon.

20. How is the Arabic word ذُرَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. sukkar
   B. dhura
   C. bataatis
   D. khudaar

21. What does the ending -aani show in yadaani? (1 mark)
   A. exactly two
   B. many
   C. the
   D. my

22. What does the Arabic sentence جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have two hands.
   B. My body is strong.
   C. This is my body.
   D. I have two eyes.

23. Which is a non-verbal cue? (1 mark)
   A. A spelling
   B. A dictionary
   C. A title
   D. A gesture

24. Which Arabic word means "river"? (1 mark)
   A. شَمْسٌ
   B. نَهْرٌ
   C. سَمَاءٌ
   D. مَطَرٌ

25. What is the name of the Arabic letter س? (1 mark)
   A. Daad
   B. qaaf
   C. zaay
   D. siin

26. Which day has the letter jiim in its name? (1 mark)
   A. al-khamiis
   B. as-sabt
   C. al-ahad
   D. al-jumuʿa

27. What does the Arabic sentence عِنْدِي هَدِيَّةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. We dance.
   B. I have a gift.
   C. I like the party.
   D. My mother cooks the food.

28. What does the Arabic word عَصِيرٌ (ʿasiir) mean? (1 mark)
   A. your turn
   B. no
   C. juice
   D. candle

29. What does the Arabic word نَعَمْ (naʿam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. congratulations
   B. my turn
   C. yes
   D. balloon

30. Which Arabic word means "milk"? (1 mark)
   A. مَوْزٌ
   B. حَلِيبٌ
   C. جَزَرٌ
   D. مَاءٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why your family members are important to you. Give two examples of roles. (3 marks) (3 marks)

32. Translate into English: uhibbu l-ʿasiira (2 marks)

33. Translate into English: al-jawwu ghaa'im (2 marks)

34. Explain why we celebrate special occasions and how pictures help us to understand a text. (3 marks) (3 marks)

35. Translate into English: uhibbu baytii (2 marks)

36. Translate into English: al-kursiyyu jadiid (2 marks)

37. Give two tips for pronouncing Arabic greetings correctly. (2 marks) (2 marks)

38. Translate into English: al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila (2 marks)

39. Translate into English: asmaʿu bi-udhunii (2 marks)

40. Translate into English: ʿindii akh wa ukht (2 marks)

41. Describe how to make a vocabulary bank of words about the home. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Introduce yourself in Arabic (English letters are fine) with your name, that you are a pupil and that you are from Kenya, then give the English meaning. (4 marks) (4 marks)

43. Write the Arabic greeting for 'peace be upon you' in English letters and give the reply. (2 marks) (2 marks)

44. Translate into English: ʿindii hadiyya (2 marks)

45. Write the seven days of the week in Arabic sounds, in order. (4 marks) (4 marks)

46. Translate into English: al-jawwu haarr (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt. (2 marks) (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: anaa fii S-Saffi r-raabiʿ (2 marks)

49. Translate into English: uhibbu l-mawza (2 marks)

50. Translate into English: ummii tatbukhu T-taʿaam (2 marks)

51. Write three body parts in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — welcome
   أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا (ahlan wa sahlan) means welcome.

2. C — The letter mim is said twice
   A shadda doubles the sound of a letter, so we say um-m.

3. C — fawqa
   fawqa means above. taHta means under, fii means in and ʿalaa means on.

4. A — house
   بَيْتٌ (bayt) means house.

5. A — ismaʿ
   اِسْمَعْ is read ismaʿ and means listen.

6. B — There are seven days in a week.
   فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ (fii l-usbuuʿi sabʿatu ayyaam) means: There are seven days in a week.

7. D — balloon
   بَالُونٌ (baaluun) means balloon.

8. C — Do you like bananas?
   هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟ (hal tuhibbu l-mawz?) means: Do you like bananas?

9. C — aghmiD ʿaynayka
   أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ is read aghmiD ʿaynayka and means close your eyes.

10. B — come in
   ادْخُلْ (udkhul) means come in.

11. D — How is the weather today?
   كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ (kayfa l-jawwu l-yawm?) means: How is the weather today?

12. C — The water is clean.
   الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ (al-maa'u nadhiif) means: The water is clean.

13. A — nuun
   The letter ن is called nuun.

14. D — ni
   نِ is read ni.

15. D — ث (thaa)
   Thaa has three dots above. Baa has one dot below and taa has two dots above.

16. A — أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ
   أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ (azuuru jaddatii yawma l-jumuʿa) means: I visit my grandmother on Friday.

17. A — dawruka
   دَوْرُكَ is read dawruka and means your turn.

18. C — فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ بَالُونٌ
   فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ بَالُونٌ (fawqa t-taawilati baaluun) means: Above the table there is a balloon.

19. C — This is a party.
   هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ (haadhihi hafla) means: This is a party.

20. B — dhura
   ذُرَةٌ is read dhura and means maize.

21. A — exactly two
   The dual ending -aani means two, so yadaani is two hands.

22. B — My body is strong.
   جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ (jismii qawiyy) means: My body is strong.

23. D — A gesture
   Gestures, facial expressions and body movements are non-verbal cues.

24. B — نَهْرٌ
   نَهْرٌ (nahr) means river.

25. D — siin
   The letter س is called siin.

26. D — al-jumuʿa
   الجمعة contains jiim (ج).

27. B — I have a gift.
   عِنْدِي هَدِيَّةٌ (ʿindii hadiyya) means: I have a gift.

28. C — juice
   عَصِيرٌ (ʿasiir) means juice.

29. C — yes
   نَعَمْ (naʿam) means yes.

30. B — حَلِيبٌ
   حَلِيبٌ (haliib) means milk.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: They love and care for us. For example parents work, cook and pay for school; grandparents share stories and advice; children help at home.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for love and care, 2 marks for two correct roles.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like juice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is cloudy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Celebrations bring people together and give joy. Pictures show what a text is about and act as clues to new words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for celebrations and 2 marks for pictures as clues.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like my house.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: The chair is new.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the teacher first and copy; say long vowels for longer than short vowels; practise the throat sounds kh and ʿ.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible tip.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: The lamp is above the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: I hear with my ear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a brother and a sister.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each Arabic word on a card with a picture; write the sound and meaning on the back; keep the cards in a box or on a chart and use them to practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: ismii Wanjiku. anaa tilmiidha. anaa min Kiiniya. My name is Wanjiku. I am a pupil. I am from Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for the meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: as-salaamu ʿalaykum. The reply is wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the greeting and 1 mark for the correct reply.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a gift.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: al-ahad, al-ithnayn, ath-thulaathaa', al-arbiʿaa', al-khamiis, al-jumuʿa, as-sabt.
   Working / marking points: 4 marks for all seven in order; 3 for five or six; 2 for three or four; 1 for one or two.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: I help my mother on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'I help my mother' and 1 mark for 'on Saturday'.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am in Grade 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: My mother cooks the food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), yad (hand), fam (mouth).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.
